questions.stem: Where do the sensitivity labels you apply to Fabric items come from?

options.text: Label files stored in the Git repository connected to the workspace
The capacity settings
Each workspace's own label list, defined by its workspace admin
Labels your organization publishes centrally for the whole tenant

questions.explanation: Fabric uses the sensitivity labels an organization publishes for its tenant.

questions.stem: At Harbor Health, a lakehouse carries the Confidential label. A semantic model and report are built on it. What can happen to their labels?

options.text: Labels never move from one item to another, so each one must be set on every item by hand
Downstream inheritance can apply the label to items built from the labeled item
The report is deleted until an owner applies the same label to it
The lakehouse loses its label once other items are built on top of it

questions.explanation: With downstream inheritance, items created from a labeled item can receive its label, so protection follows the data.

questions.stem: A user exports data from a labeled Power BI report to Excel. What happens to the label?

options.text: The label is applied to the exported file, where the export format supports it
The label is written as plain text in cell A1 of the first worksheet
The label is always dropped on export, so the Excel file leaves Fabric unprotected
Export is always blocked

questions.explanation: Labels persist on supported exports such as Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, so the file stays protected outside Fabric.

questions.stem: Users can't see any sensitivity labels to apply in Fabric. What must be in place?

options.text: A Git connection on the workspace, which syncs the label list from the connected repository
A custom Spark pool
Published sensitivity labels and the Fabric admin setting that lets users apply them
A deployment pipeline whose stage settings publish labels to the workspace

questions.explanation: Labels must be defined and published for the organization, and a Fabric admin must turn on the tenant setting that allows users to apply them.

questions.stem: A lakehouse labeled General is loaded from an upstream item labeled Highly Confidential. Which label does an item autogenerated from the lakehouse get through downstream inheritance?

options.text: The tenant's default label only
Highly Confidential, from the item further upstream
General, from its parent lakehouse
No label until someone sets one

questions.explanation: Autogenerated items take their label from their parent lakehouse or warehouse, not from items further upstream.

questions.stem: A lakehouse carries the Confidential label. An engineer creates a new notebook from the lakehouse. What label does the notebook get?

options.text: No label
Confidential, inherited from the lakehouse when it's created
Confidential, but only after the notebook's first run
The tenant default label

questions.explanation: Inheritance upon creation gives a notebook created from a lakehouse the lakehouse's label at the moment it's created.

questions.stem: Mandatory labeling is on and default labeling is off. A user creates a lakehouse. What can happen?

options.text: The user can save the lakehouse without a label, because mandatory labeling isn't enforced for lakehouses
The lakehouse can't be created at all until a Fabric admin also turns on default labeling for the whole tenant
The lakehouse automatically gets the organization's highest-priority label when it is saved
The user must pick a label before saving, exactly as for Power BI reports and semantic models

questions.explanation: Mandatory labeling is fully supported only for Power BI items. For lakehouses, pipelines and warehouses, the logic isn't enforced.

questions.stem: An admin must apply a sensitivity label to hundreds of existing lakehouses and pipelines at once. What supports this?

options.text: Committing them to Git with the label in the commit message
Downstream inheritance from a semantic model
Labeling them programmatically through the Power BI admin REST APIs
A deployment rule on each stage

questions.explanation: Programmatic labeling is supported for all Fabric items and lets labels be added, changed or deleted through the admin REST APIs.

questions.stem: A user creates a new pipeline through its normal create dialog and doesn't choose a label. A default label policy is in place. What happens?

options.text: The pipeline is saved with no label
The create dialog blocks saving
The default sensitivity label is applied to the pipeline
The pipeline gets the label of the workspace's most sensitive item

questions.explanation: For non-Power BI items created through a clear create dialog, the default label is applied if the user doesn't choose one.

questions.stem: A deployment pipeline deploys a labeled item to the next stage. In which two cases is the sensitivity label copied to the target item? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A new item is deployed, or an item is deployed to an empty stage
Only when a deployment rule names the label
The source item has a label with protection and the target item doesn't
Every deployment, whatever the labels are
The target item has a higher label than the source

questions.explanation: Labels are copied only for new items or deployments to an empty stage, and when the source has a protected label the target lacks (after consent). Otherwise the target keeps its label.
